From: Alex Hwang <alex@emberlyx.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for clinical-inference — context 32k / need sizing guidance

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap of Emberlyx's ask: we want dedicated GPU capacity to serve a medical summarization workflow for clinical notes. Primary constraints:
- Model candidates: Mistral-7B (base), Llama-2-13B, and a custom 16B finetune (FP16 checkpoints).
- Typical request: 10 concurrent sessions, average prompt+response length ~6k tokens, occasional peak sessions up to 25k tokens (long threads).
- SLA: p95 latency under 600ms for responses after generation starts; throughput target ~12 responses/minute sustained.
- Security: VPC private deployment hooked into your Dedicated offering.

Can you provide a sizing guidance that includes: GPU count by model variant, expected headroom for KV cache at 8k/32k, and recommended quantization profile (bf16/FP16/4-bit q4) with expected memory and latency tradeoffs?

Would appreciate a short spreadsheet and any quick rules of thumb.

—Alex
Alex Hwang
Platform Eng, Emberlyx

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Emberlyx sizing — initial numbers and ask for calc

Markus / Monica — attached is the quick simulation (kv_cache_simulation.csv) and a short note. Summary of our conservative planning assumptions (rounded numbers):

Assumptions and per-GPU resident sizes (estimate):
- Mistral-7B FP16: model weights ~14 GB (FP16), runtime workspace + activations ~6 GB, KV cache per token ~0.5 KB/token -> KV for 8k ≈ 4 MB? (see note below), for 32k ≈ 16 MB. Full resident w/8k = ~20 GB; w/32k = ~36 GB.
- Llama-2-13B FP16: model weights ~26 GB, runtime workspace ~10 GB, KV cache per token ~0.9 KB/token -> 8k ≈ 7.2 MB, 32k ≈ 28.8 MB. Full resident w/8k ≈ 37 GB; w/32k ≈ 58 GB.
- Custom-16B FP16: model weights ~32 GB, runtime workspace ~12 GB, KV cache per token ~1.1 KB/token -> 8k ≈ 8.8 MB, 32k ≈ 35.2 MB. Full resident w/8k ≈ 53 GB; w/32k ≈ 86 GB.

Important: the KV cache numbers above are conservative rounded MB-level estimates — in practice KV is a few bytes per token per key/value vector per layer; our simulation translates those into MB to produce per-GPU headroom numbers. The dominant driver is base weights + activations for larger models, while KV scales linearly with sequence length.

Quantization tradeoffs (impact on resident memory and latency):
- q4_0 (symmetric 4-bit): reduces model weight footprint by ~2.7–3x vs FP16; expected latency hit on generation ~+10–20% depending on kernels.
- q4_1 (improved layout): similar ~3x weight reduction with slightly better latency (~+5–12%).
- bf16 vs FP16: similar memory; bf16 preferred on some HW for speed but not a memory win.

Sizing recommendation (conservative, 15% headroom, target steady 10 concurrent, peak 30):
- Mistral-7B FP16 (cost-efficient): 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs in a small dedicated pod (each GPU can host ~3 steady sessions at 8k with headroom; at 32k the same pod supports ~1 session/GPU). For q4_1 this becomes approx 10 steady sessions / 4 GPUs (fits steady load) but latency may increase slightly on long contexts.
- Llama-2-13B FP16: 6 x A100-40GB equivalent GPUs for steady 10 sessions at 32k headroom; if Emberlyx chooses q4_1 we can fit steady 10 sessions on 4 GPUs but recommend 6 for burst x3 headroom and rolling updates.
- Custom-16B FP16: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs for 32k headroom; with q4_1 this drops to 4-5 GPUs but we recommend reserving 6 for safe autoscale and A/B testing.

Operational notes:
- For 32k contexts we recommend dedicated KV-cache pinned nodes per model variant to avoid cross-tenant eviction and to improve cold-start latency.
- Enable automatic prefix caching for repeated patient templates to dramatically reduce effective KV sizes for common patterns.
- For cost savings, offer a heterogenous pool: reserve N GPUs for FP16 high-performance (burst & low-latency) and M GPUs quantized for steady cheap throughput with automatic fallback if latency SLOs are missed.

I attached the CSV with the per-token sweep. Let me know any tweaks.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Alex — attaching a short proposal (redwood_capacity_note.pdf) and the simulation CSV. TL;DR recommendation tailored to your goals:

Recommendation (what to order):
- Pilot (6 weeks): 4 x A100-40GB (dedicated pool) running Llama-2-13B in q4_1 for steady work. Rationale: q4_1 gives ~3x memory reduction so 13B fits comfortably with 32k contexts and preserves most throughput with modest latency uplift. This keeps cost moderate and lets you validate latency/quality on real clinical data.
- Production (if pilot looks good): scale to 6 x A100-40GB for primary capacity and add 2 x A40-equivalents as burst/quantized nodes to offload very long-tail jobs and lower-priority batch inference.

Operational checklist and next steps:
- Confirm whether you want us to create a heterogenous pool (we'll include an autoscale policy and a fallback route to quantized nodes).
- We'll provide a HIPAA addendum for Dedicated Private deployment; need PoC network details.
- We'll run a small A/B evaluation (FP16 vs q4_1) on your sample dataset — requires the signed NDA and test keys.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough Tuesday to go over the attached sheet.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: emberlyx_model_profile.xlsx (model inventory), kv_cache_simulation.csv (token-by-token sweep), redwood_capacity_note.pdf (proposal)
